newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo bourse hits new high but market seen fragile.
newsitem.headline: Oslo bourse hits new high but market seen fragile.

text.p: Norwegian stocks traded to a new all-time high on Wednesday led by new records on other European bourses, but dealers said the market was in a delicate balance.

"We move up if Wall Street and Europe go up, but the market in Norway is fragile, partly because we've made such big gains in the last year but also because of worries over the economy and inflation," said one dealer. "Small negative news will have much more of an impact that positive news."
Oslo's Total share index climbed 1.1 percent to close at 1.278.51 points in relatively healthy turnover of 986 million crowns.
Dealers said sentiment for offshore stocks remained positive, with prices rising in relatively active trade.
Procon Offshore, recently spun off from Transocean Offshore, advanced 3.5 percent to 74.50 crowns in turnover of 37 million crowns, while Hydralift gained 7.6 percent to 240 crowns.

Of the blue chips, oil company Saga climbed 3.45 percent to 150 crowns on expectations of successful drilling results in Norwegian waters, and drugs company Nycomed attracted overseas buying on rumours of a new analyst report. Nycomed closed two percent up at 148 crowns.
